skill.name: doubt-driven-development
skill.description: Subjects every non-trivial decision to a fresh-context adversarial review before it stands. Use when you want every assumption cross-examined before proceeding, when stress-testing a plan for hidden failure modes, when correctness matters more than speed, when working in unfamiliar code, when stakes are high (production auth, security-sensitive logic, a high-stakes migration, irreversible operations), or any time a confident output would be cheaper to verify now than to debug later.
skill.summary: Applies bounded, fresh-context adversarial review to non-trivial engineering decisions before they stand.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, ordinary prose, or documentation links. The fixed files in /tmp create local confidentiality and integrity risk, while cross-model review can expose sensitive artifacts or let untrusted artifact instructions influence a CLI reviewer.

remediation.issue: The command examples use a predictable shared temporary file for review prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Create the prompt with mktemp, restrict permissions to the current user, quote the generated path, and remove the file after review.

remediation.issue: Cross-model review can expose sensitive content and gives untrusted artifacts to an agent that may read the repository.
remediation.suggestion: Require a secrets and data-policy check, isolate the artifact from the repository, disable network access, and state that artifact instructions are untrusted.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Artifact Disclosure to External Models
semantic_findings.description: The workflow offers to send artifacts and contracts to external model CLIs without requiring a secrets, ownership, or data-retention check. User authorization for execution does not establish that the content may leave its trust boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly offers Gemini or Codex review and specifies which artifact content to submit. It discusses authorization and credentials but not content sensitivity or provider policy.

semantic_findings.title: Incomplete Isolation for Prompt-Injected Artifacts
semantic_findings.description: The skill recognizes that artifacts may contain prompt injection but treats a read-only sandbox as sufficient containment. A reviewer launched inside the repository may still read sensitive files or use network capabilities, depending on the CLI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples launch model CLIs with the repository as context, and the text explicitly anticipates prompt injection. Read-only access protects writes but does not universally prevent reads or outbound disclosure.

content.user_title: Challenge Engineering Decisions Before They Stand
content.value_statement: Long sessions can turn assumptions into accepted facts and hide costly failure modes. This skill applies bounded, fresh-context adversarial review before non-trivial decisions stand.
actual_capabilities: Identifies non-trivial decisions that warrant adversarial review.
Separates the artifact and contract from the author's original claim.
Creates an issues-focused prompt for a fresh-context reviewer.
Classifies findings as contract errors, actionable issues, accepted trade-offs, or noise.
Limits review to three cycles before user escalation.
Offers user-authorized cross-model review during interactive sessions.
limitations: Fresh-context reviewers can miss constraints that are absent from the contract.
Cross-model review adds cost, latency, configuration requirements, and possible data exposure.
Nested subagent restrictions can reduce the process to less reliable self-questioning.
The skill improves scrutiny but cannot prove correctness or replace testing.

use_cases.title: Validate an Architecture Decision
use_cases.description: Challenge service boundaries, shared state, failure modes, and unstated assumptions before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review Security-Sensitive Logic
use_cases.description: Test authentication, authorization, or data-handling changes against an explicit contract before committing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a High-Risk Migration
use_cases.description: Expose irreversible steps, rollback gaps, and hidden dependencies before approving a production migration.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply doubt-driven development to this decision. State the claim, extract the artifact and contract, then find assumptions and failure modes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a structured review of one non-trivial decision.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a Code Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change against its contract. Focus on edge cases, hidden state, broken conventions, and inputs that violate expected behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer has a focused diff or function ready for review.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Reviewer Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify each finding as contract misread, actionable issue, accepted trade-off, or noise. Cite artifact evidence and recommend the next step.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs to evaluate adversarial feedback without accepting it automatically.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Bounded Review Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Run up to three doubt cycles on this high-stakes artifact. Track changed assumptions, unresolved findings, accepted trade-offs, and the final stop condition.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs traceable review before an irreversible change.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal to add shared in-memory caching to a concurrent service.
output: Claim: The cache remains correct under concurrent reads and writes.
Actionable issue: The proposal does not define synchronization during eviction.
Next step: Specify the concurrency contract and rerun the review.

output_examples.input: Challenge a database migration plan that removes a legacy column.
output: Contract misread: The rollback window was not included in the supplied contract.
Actionable issue: Older application instances still read the legacy column.
Stop status: Revise the deployment order before another review cycle.

output_examples.input: Reconcile feedback about a public API pagination change.
output_examples.output: Accepted trade-off: Existing clients keep the old default for one release. Document the compatibility period and add a removal checkpoint.

best_practices: Keep each artifact small and provide a precise contract.
Use reviewer findings as evidence, then verify each finding against the artifact.
Record the stop condition and escalate unresolved issues after three cycles.
anti_patterns: Do not pass the original claim when independent contract evaluation is required.
Do not invoke external model tools without explicit authorization for each call.
Do not repeat reviews on an unchanged artifact to manufacture confidence.

faq.question: How is this different from a final code review?
faq.answer: It challenges non-trivial decisions during development, while a final review evaluates a completed artifact.

faq.question: What counts as a non-trivial decision?
faq.answer: Examples include branching logic, module boundaries, unverifiable invariants, irreversible changes, and decisions with hidden context.

faq.question: Does every change need a doubt cycle?
faq.answer: No. Mechanical edits, formatting, simple file moves, and obvious one-line changes usually do not need one.

faq.question: Must I use another model?
faq.answer: No. Interactive sessions should offer cross-model review, but the user may skip it.

faq.question: When should the review loop stop?
faq.answer: Stop after trivial findings, three cycles, or an explicit user decision to proceed.

faq.question: Can reviewer findings be accepted automatically?
faq.answer: No. Recheck every finding against the artifact and classify it before changing the work.
